'''Lily Signe Khadjavi''', professor of mathematics at [[Loyola Marymount University]], is an American mathematician known for her work on the mathematics of social justice.

==Education==

Khadjavi earned a PhD from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1999. Her dissertation, in [[number theory]], was titled ''An Effective Version Of Belyi's Theorem'' and her doctoral advisor was [[Hendrik Lenstra]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Lily Signe Khadjavi |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=38200 |website=Mathematics Genealogy Project |access-date=6 April 2022}}</ref>

==Books==

Khadjavi and [[Gizem Karaali]] have co-edited two books, ''Mathematics for Social Justice: Resources for the College Classroom'' and ''Mathematics for Social Justice: Focusing on Quantitative Reasoning and Statistics'', which provide resources for mathematics instructors who want to add social justice topics to their courses or create new mathematics courses centered around social justice. The books are published by the [[Mathematical Association of America|MAA]] Press, an imprint of the American Mathematical Society.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mathematics for Social Justice: Resources for the College Classroom and Focusing on Quantitative Reasoning and Statistics (2-Volume Set) |url=https://bookstore.ams.org/cdn-1639207548218/clrm-karaali-set/ |website=AMS Bookstore |publisher=American Mathematical Society |access-date=6 April 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Edholm |first1=Christina |title=Mathematics for Social Justice: An Interview with the Editors |journal=MAA Focus |date=July 2020 |url=http://digitaleditions.walsworthprintgroup.com/publication/?i=663226&article_id=3695296&view=articleBrowser |access-date=6 April 2022}}</ref> In a personal essay, Karaali has described taking inspiration from Khadjavi's work on [[racial profiling]] in Los Angeles-area traffic stops when teaching an interdisciplinary first-year seminar.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Karaali |first1=Gizem |title=Humanistic Mathematics: An Oxymoron? |journal=Diversity & Democracy |date=Spring 2012 |volume=15 |issue=2 |page=21 |url=https://scholarship.claremont.edu/pomona_fac_pub/167/ |access-date=6 April 2022}}</ref>

==Professional service==

Khadjavi is a member of the board of [[Spectra (mathematical association)|Spectra]], the association for LGBTQ+ mathematicians, and a member at large on the council of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Spectra Board |url=http://lgbtmath.org/Board.html |website=Spectra |access-date=6 April 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Council |url=https://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/council/member-council |website=American Mathematical Society |access-date=6 April 2022}}</ref> In 2020, California Attorney General [[Xavier Becerra]] appointed her to the state of California's Racial and Identity Profiling Advisory Board, which was established to address racial and identity-based profiling by law enforcement.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mathematics Professor Appointed to State Board on Racial Profiling |url=https://newsroom.lmu.edu/campusnews/mathematics-professor-appointed-to-state-board-on-racial-profiling/ |website=Campus News |date=6 October 2020 |publisher=Loyola Marymount University |access-date=6 April 2022}}</ref> In January of 2023, Khadjavi received the Mary and Alfie Gray Award for Social Justice, presented by the Association of Women in Mathematics (AWM).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boucher |first=Noémie |date=2023-04-14 |title=LMU Mathematician Honored with National Social Justice Award |url=https://newsroom.lmu.edu/campusnews/lmu-mathematician-honored-with-national-social-justice-award/ |access-date=2026-09-05 |website=Loyola Marymount University Newsroom |language=en-US}}</ref>

Khadjavi has presented her work as [[popular science]] and in context of social issues.<ref name="Knudson 2021">{{cite web |last1=Knudson |first1=Kevin |title=Episode 63 - Lily Khadjavi |url=https://kpknudson.com/my-favorite-theorem/2021/2/11/episode-63-lily-khadjavi |website=My Favorite Theorem |format=podcast |date=February 11, 2021}}</ref>
